title: No charges laid in 2016 officer-involved shooting, despite ASIRT recommendation to Crown
article: Despite the fact no charges will be laid, a Calgary police officer who shot and killed a man driving erratically in a parkade may not have been justified in doing so, a police watchdog report read.

The shooting took place in an Inglewood parkade on July 15, 2016 when a man, later identified by friends as 41-year-old Sanjai Prasad, was shot dead by police officer who fired a police-issued C8 Carbine.

The incident was a complicated one, Alberta Serious Incident Response Team executive director Sue Hughson said, as the subject officer engaged his constitutional right to remain silent in the investigation.

"The absence of evidence regarding the involved officer's perception of the events and articulation of reasons why lethal force was reasonably necessary in the circumstances left a vacuum that was complicated by the unexplained decision to use the C8 patrol rifle to search the parkade," Hughson said.

While Hughson forwarded her report with reasonable grounds to believe that an offence had been committed to the Crown, the Crown felt the evidence presented "did not meet the standard for prosecution, finding there was no reasonable likelihood of conviction."

The gun involved, a C8 patrol rifle, is used by Calgary police "for situations where an officer may face armed and/or ballistically protected suspects," Hughson said, adding the weapon's use "could have been arguably contrary to CPS policy and could be interpreted as an overly aggressive response to the call as dispatched;" this, given the tight corridors, the fact there was only one officer who fired, and that the offences alleged to have been committed were "on the minor end of the scale of criminal offences," Hughson said.

The incident started when Calgary police responded to an apartment complex near 17th Ave. and 17 St. S.E. at 7:52 p.m. for reports of four people acting suspiciously in the parkade, possibly trying to access vehicles. The day before, the property management company posted a security bulletin about four people who broke into the garage.
The caller reported seeing a person they believed to have been in the bulletin.
Evidence put Prasad and three others along with a stolen silver Hyundai SUV inside the parkade allegedly in search of a licence plate to put on the SUV, Hughson said.
Six officers entered the parkade at 7:57 p.m. with three entering the east side, one of whom was the involved officer qualified to carry a C8, and another three entering the west side.

Prasad, who was found to have methamphetamine metabolites in his system during a subsequent toxicology report Hughson said, was found by officers on the west end of the parkade "circling in the parkade (and) appeared to be looking for the exit."

When officers made contact, attempting to stop the vehicle, it neared a dead-end, Hughson said, before the vehicle was put into reverse rapidly accelerating as it smashed into a parked Jeep, pushing it 3.3 metres.
While one man fled from the vehicle to be arrested a short time later, Prasad drove away as officers called in their code for officer in trouble, Hughson said.
The vehicle began to drive towards the east side of the parkade , Hughson said, before having to swerve to avoid two of the three officers running towards the west side of the parkade.

"With respect to the involved officer, the evidence established that as the silver Hyundai progressed down the lane in his direction, he discharged his C8 patrol rifle," Hughson said, before firing five times in under two seconds.
Prasad was immediately found dead as police took the two other passengers into custody.
The male passenger still inside the vehicle described that at one point, Prasad said, "this is it for me," then screamed, "I'm sorry."

After the shooting, a Postmedia source described Prasad, nicknamed "kilo," as "a nightmare wherever he goes," and criminal records out of Alberta and B.C. show offences including extortion, fraud, drugs, weapons, resisting arrest and violence, including spousal assault.
